QF.id: SEBI Guidelines for AML Standards, CFT and PF with KYC Norms_29

question.text: What does SEBI expect intermediaries to do to build staff awareness on AML/CFT?

answer.text: Ensure staff understand AML/CFT directives, can identify, monitor and report suspected ML/TF transactions, and maintain awareness and vigilance — including front-line staff
Restrict AML/CFT knowledge to the Principal Officer only
Outsource the entire AML/CFT function so internal staff do not need awareness
Limit AML/CFT awareness to back-office settlement staff only

explanation.text: The Logic: Intermediaries must ensure that AML/CFT directives are understood by staff, that there are systems for identifying, monitoring and reporting suspected ML/TF transactions, and that staff awareness and vigilance — including front-line staff awareness and responsibilities — are developed. The Trap: AML/CFT awareness cannot be confined to one officer, outsourced wholesale, or limited to back-office staff. Front-line interaction is specifically called out in the source. Note: Build directive-comprehension, suspicious-transaction identification, and reporting capability across roles, with particular focus on front-line staff who interact directly with clients.
